headline: Civil Service Commission picks top four for public director interviews

meeting.body: Maui Civil Service Commission Advances DPS Director Search
meeting.summary: The Civil Service Commission voted to interview its top four director candidates in public, with interviews expected to start the week of September 28.
meeting.recap: No one gave public testimony.[[0:01:27]] The Civil Service Commission worked on the timeline and process for choosing a new department director.[[0:01:48]] The commission voted to interview the top four candidates instead of six.[[0:29:30]] If no candidates are left, the commission will meet again to decide next steps.[[0:35:18]] A commissioner said OIP advised against using executive session, a closed-door discussion, for the interviews.[[0:39:47]] The vice chair read an email from an absent commissioner who favored interviews by the full commission.[[0:44:56]] Commissioners want to cut the 24-question reference questionnaire down to 10 questions.[[1:08:45]] Commissioners plan to meet on the 26th from 9 to 12 to finish the packet.[[1:31:22]] A rough timeline has interviews starting the week of September 28.[[1:37:24]] The 29th and 30th of September were held as possible interview dates.[[1:56:41]] The meeting was adjourned by voice vote.[[2:01:34]]
decided: The commission approved interviewing the top four instead of six by voice vote.
The commission approved limiting replacements to candidates ranked down to six by voice vote.
meeting.next: A commissioner will draft the candidate cover letter with dates left blank, working with corporation counsel. The commission will research whether it can require candidates to interview in person. Commissioners will bring their edits and a to-do list to the meeting on the 26th. A special meeting with resource people, such as the former director, may be held before the interviews.
